item.title: Reps pass vote of confidence in Tinubu, NNPC boss
item.description: •Dismiss money laundering petition against EVP By Gift ChapiOdekina Abuja—The House of Representatives Committee on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) has dismissed a petition alleging conflict of interest and money laundering against NNPC’s Executive Vice President (Downstream), Dr. Mumuni Dagazau, saying the petitioners failed to provide documentary evidence to substantiate their claims. It also passed a vote of confidence on President Bola Tinubu and the Group Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, NNPCL, citing improvements in domestic refining, crude oil supply and stability in the downstream petroleum sector. Chairman of the committee, Ikenga Imo Ugochinyere, announced the decisions during proceedings on pending matters and the federal government’s downstream sector reforms in Abuja yesterday. Ugochinyere said the committee’s decision followed a review of its subcommittee’s report, which found that the petitioners, the Coalition for Transparency and Accountability in Nigeria’s Petroleum Sector, failed to substantiate their allegations against Dagazau. According to him, the petitioners appeared before the subcommittee on October 21 but presented newspaper clippings rather than documentary evidence to support allegations as serious as money laundering. He said they were given further opportunities to provide supporting documents but failed to return on Thursday and Friday, October 22 and 23. On the other hand, he said Dagazau honoured the committee’s invitation through his representatives, who responded to the inquiries raised by the subcommittee. “An allegation is not evidence, and a newspaper clipping is not proof,” Ugochinyere said, announcing the dismissal of the petition in its entirety. The committee chairman condemned what he described as a frivolous petition, warning that the National Assembly would not allow its oversight proceedings to become a platform for unsubstantiated attacks on public officials. He, however, maintained that the committee remained open to investigating allegations of wrongdoing against public officers where credible evidence was provided. The committee also granted its subcommittee investigating NIPCO Plc an additional 14 days to conclude its assignment. Reps reject blanket fuel subsidy return On the contentious issue of fuel subsidy, the committee chairman argued that a return to the former nationwide subsidy regime would impose a significant burden on public finances. He said Nigerians consumed about 50 million litres of petrol daily and that, based on the federal government’s estimates, restoring the former pump price would cost more than N20 trillion annually. According to him, such expenditure will approach the total amount shared among the federal, state and local governments through the Federation Account in 2025. “A blanket subsidy does not lower the cost of fuel; it only changes who pays, and when,” he said. item.title: 2027 Campaign Billboards: How states are pricing opposition out of sight
item.description: *APM fights back, goes to court *We’re not discriminating against any party – States *It can cream off 80% of allowed campaign limit By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – A growing number of state governments are charging presidential candidates tens and even hundreds of millions of naira for the right to display posters and billboards, raising fears that visibility is being priced beyond the reach of opposition parties less than three months to the January 16, 2027 election. Campaigns for the Presidential and National Assembly polls opened on August 19. By then, several states had already published fee schedules, and the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, had cleared 19 presidential candidates. Abia sets the highest rate. Its signage agency charges N200 million for a presidential candidate, N150 million for a governorship candidate, N100 million for a senatorial candidate, N50 million for the House of Representatives and N20 million for the State Assembly. Enugu and Kogi each demand N150 million from presidential candidates. Cross River is reported at N150 million, Rivers at N75 million and Anambra at N50 million, a five-fold rise on its 2022 presidential fee of N10 million. The contrast with other states shows how arbitrary the figures are. Kano charges about N1.15 million and draws no distinction between political and commercial billboards. Kaduna assesses fees site by site. Imo asks senatorial candidates for N5 million, plus application and inspection charges. A question of arithmetic The sums matter because of the spending ceiling in the Electoral Act 2026, which caps a presidential candidate’s election expenses at N10 billion and a governorship candidate’s at N3 billion. If Abia’s N200 million applied in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, permits alone would cost N7.4 billion, or 74 per cent of the presidential cap, before a single rally, jingle or vehicle is paid for. The Allied Peoples Movement, APM, and its presidential candidate, Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, argue that such fees could consume more than 80 per cent of the ceiling. They have asked the Abia High Court in suit HC/214/2026 to declare the N200 million fee unconstitutional and void. No hearing date had been announced at the last report, and no court has ruled on the legality of any of these fees. Not simply an APC tyranny The opposition has described the fees as a ruling-party tactic. The African Democratic Congress, ADC, said they are targeted at the opposition and has vowed to challenge them. The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, said the states involved are mostly controlled by the All Progressives Congress, APC. But the record is more complicated. The N200 million fee in Abia was imposed by the administration of Governor Alex Otti of the Labour Party, LP. In Oyo, the APC accuses the APM-led state government of directing its signage agency to clamp down on non-APM campaigners. item.title: NESG: We’re rewriting Nigeria’s story of under-performance — Tinubu
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu said yesterday that his administration is rewriting Nigeria’s decades-long story of economic under-performance through far-reaching reforms designed to dismantle structural barriers, unlock the nation’s enormous potential and deliver jobs, productivity and shared prosperity. He also said the administration is currently undertaking what it came into office to achieve — rewriting the story of a nation that had performed below its potential for far too long. Speaking when he formally declared open the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit Group, NESG, in Abuja yesterday, President Tinubu, who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, noted that his administration began on a difficult note because there was no shortcut to economic growth. “We came to rewrite the story of a nation that has performed below its potential for far too long. But there is no shortcut to economic growth. This is why we began with a difficult reset. For us, rescuing the economy means rescuing livelihoods and transforming the fortunes of young job seekers, farmers, manufacturers, entrepreneurs and innovators. “We cannot harness the immense opportunities offered by our growing population without first stabilising the economy. We must also create the conditions for the public and private sectors to invest, expand and generate productive employment,” he explained. Tinubu observed that the summit’s theme, “Growth That Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity,” was built on the ambition of the previous edition of the annual event to achieve a prosperous and inclusive Nigeria by 2030. He noted that his administration had “since set in motion a series of reforms to dismantle the structural barriers that have prevented our abundant human and natural resources from yielding prosperity. “These reforms are restoring confidence, strengthening our economic foundations and laying the groundwork for sustainable growth.” The President noted that the administration was encouraged by what it had accomplished so far, acknowledging that creating jobs was only half the task. ‘Need to improve quality of work’ While noting there is need to improve the quality of work, reduce underemployment and harness the potential of the country’s under-utilised workforce, Tinubu said: “Our pursuit of prosperity demands greater productivity from every worker, enterprise and investment. We must judge infrastructure by the economic activity it generates and education by the skills and productivity it delivers. “We must judge industrial policy by the competitiveness of our firms and investment incentives by the capital, technology, exports and jobs they attract.” The President outlined what he described as the achievements of his administration’s reforms, saying they had been well-documented. item.title: Abia PDP guber candidate, Anosike, vows common facility centre for Aba leather, garment clusters
item.description: The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, governorship candidate for the 2027 election in Abia State, Dr. Kelechi Anosike, has promised to build a world-class Common Facility Centre, CFC, in Aba to boost the leather and garment clusters. Anosike made the promise in Aba when he met with representatives of the Leather and Garment Clusters, comprising over 200,000 members, as part of his ongoing campaign tour of the commercial city. He said the proposed CFC would be a solar-powered industrial and technical hub equipped with world-class machines to enable Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), especially young tailors, shoemakers and garment makers who lack capital, to produce international-standard finished products. According to him, the model would replicate what the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria, SMEDAN, did in Abuja, where tailors register their materials, pay a token of N5,000, now N10,000, to access all machines in the centre to finish jobs for their customers and keep the proceeds. “I said we will set up a centre, solar powered, with all kinds of world best machines. Like what SMEDAN did in Abuja, like the tailoring aspect,” he said. The PDP candidate recalled that a similar facility built in Aba in 2008 by the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation, UNIDO, in partnership with the Federal and Abia State Governments was abused, vandalised and eventually abandoned by successive administrations, thereby defeating its empowerment purpose. He said his administration would bring back the concept as a deliberate empowerment strategy, stressing that apart from the CFC, his government would establish a Traders Microfinance Bank to provide interest-free loans and grants to traders and clusters to scale up production and reduce dependence on imports. Anosike argued that while white-collar jobs are limited, thousands of SMEs can be created if government partners with traders to produce locally made goods for which Nigeria spends over $10 to $20 billion annually importing, despite having the raw materials in abundance. Anchoring his campaign on what he termed “productive welfarism,” the governorship hopeful said his mission is encapsulated in the slogan ‘Aruo Uzo, Aruo Afo’ (build roads, build people), insisting that infrastructure is meaningless if the people are not alive and economically empowered to use it. “I’m a welfarist and the welfarism is not to give you handouts, it’s to empower you to support the state. It is called productive welfarism,” he declared. He criticised what he described as anti-people taxes on the poor, vowing to abolish them, and lamented that despite the increase in federal allocation to Abia from about N3.5 billion to about N40 billion monthly, there was “zero welfare” to cushion the effects of subsidy removal. item.title: [UPDATED] Kane Edges Yamal, Mbappe To Taste Ballon d’Or Glory
item.description: Harry Kane became England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years in his native London on Monday, beating stiff competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe. Alexia Putellas claimed the women’s prize for a third time, extending Spain’s dominance of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season’s Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses. The first-ever Ballon d’Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late. But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date. England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane smiles after receiving the Ballon d’Or award for the best male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup. “Without you guys (his Bayern Munich teammates) and the rest of the team it wouldn’t be possible; the way you guys push me, the way we compete. So thank you very much,” he said after collecting the award. Kane’s medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs since he arrived at Bayern in 2023. He was on the losing side for Tottenham in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England. Spain and Barcelona midfielder Alexia Putellas (centre) and England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane (right) pose after receiving their Ballon d’Or awards for the best female and male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) But his remarkable goalscoring consistency has earned him the highest individual award in football. “Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career,” Kane told AFP earlier. “Some people saw it as a risk, but for me it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the teammates, the team, the club, and it has pushed me onto another level. “Being a number nine for Bayern and England, you are expected to score goals and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I’m really proud of,” he added. item.title: Harry Kane crowned 2026 Ballon d’Or winner
item.description: England captain Harry Kane has been crowned the winner of the 2026 Ballon d’Or, claiming football’s most prestigious individual award. The Bayern Munich striker emerged as the standout player at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, held on Monday, October 26, after an outstanding year for club and country. Kane’s triumph marks a major milestone in his career, recognising his performances for Bayern Munich and the England national team. The England international has established himself as one of the world’s leading forwards, combining prolific goalscoring with his ability to create opportunities for teammates. His victory comes after intense competition from several leading contenders, including Paris Saint-Germain’s Ousmane Dembélé, Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé and Barcelona youngster Lamine Yamal. The Ballon d’Or, organised by France Football, recognises the best footballer over the relevant assessment period. Kane’s win adds another landmark achievement to a career that has seen him become England’s all-time leading goalscorer and one of the most prolific strikers in European football. item.title: [UPDATED] Alexia Putellas Wins 2026 Women’s Ballon d’Or
item.description: Alexia Putellas picked up her third Ballon d’Or in her new home city of London on Monday, crowning a spectacular return to the top of women’s football after injury cut her down in her prime. Putellas previously picked up the prize for the best player in the world in 2021 and 2022 as the creative heartbeat of an all-conquering Barcelona side. But an anterior cruciate ligament tear just as she was preparing for Spain’s bid to win Euro 2022 derailed her rise to global stardom. Spain and Barcelona midfielder Alexia Putellas and England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane pose with their trophies on stage after receiving their Ballon d’Or awards for the best female and male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) Putellas recovered to play a bit part role in Spain’s World Cup triumph a year later, but was overshadowed by teammate Aitana Bonmatí for both club and country as it took nearly two years to rediscover her best form. “Ever since I suffered the injury, I’ve been trying to enjoy every moment as if it were my last, because you never know if it’ll happen again,” Putellas told AFP in an interview last month. Bonmati took on the mantle of the world’s best player, becoming a three-time Ballon d’Or winner between 2023 and 2025 until she was also sidelined by a leg break. With the emphasis back on Putellas, she rose to the challenge, helping Barcelona regain the Champions League last season in dominant fashion. “I never felt that the (Ballon d’Or) trophy was ‘mine’… Having already experienced it once, I’m able to enjoy it even more now,” she added. Having achieved all that she could in Catalonia, Putellas embarked on a new adventure, joining London City Lionesses. Owned by American businesswoman Michele Kang, the Lionesses are aiming to break the mould as the only fully independent team in England’s top division. “It’s a complete change in my life. It’s a constant, daily learning process: the culture, the language, moving to a new country, a new city,” said the 32-year-old. “I knew that if I ever had to end my time at Barca, it wouldn’t make much sense to repeat what I’d already experienced in the next chapter, mainly because it’s impossible. “It had to be something completely different. It’s practically a brand-new club, with everything yet to be written, so I’m trying to bring that winning culture and mentality with me.” The Putellas effect is already being felt in the English Women’s Super League with the Lionesses sat just behind Chelsea and Manchester City at the top of the table and ahead of traditional giants Arsenal. The move could also benefit Spain’s chances of retaining the World Cup next year with their star player facing a lesser workload without European football this season. “It was one of the things I took into account. item.title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Alexia Putellas wins Best Women’s Player award for third time
item.description: Barcelona midfielder Alexia Putellas has won the 2026 Women’s Ballon d’Or, claiming the prestigious individual award for the third time in her career. The Spanish international was crowned the best women’s footballer at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, adding another major individual honour to her impressive career. Putellas, one of the most decorated players in women’s football, previously won the award in 2021 and 2022, becoming the first woman to claim the Women’s Ballon d’Or in consecutive years. Her latest triumph further strengthens her legacy as one of the leading figures in the women’s game, following years of success with Barcelona and the Spain national team. The midfielder has played a key role in Barcelona’s dominance in domestic and European competitions, earning recognition for her technical ability, creativity and leadership. Winning the award for a third time places Putellas among the most successful recipients in the history of the Women’s Ballon d’Or. item.title: Trump hits back at Obama over Saddam ‘Cheesecake Factory’ jab
item.description: US President Donald Trump hit back at Barack Obama on Monday after the former president jokingly said his successor’s White House looked as if it were a cheesecake restaurant run by Saddam Hussein. “For you to say it’s a Cheesecake Factory, that just shows why you were a lousy president,” Trump said in a three-minute diatribe when asked about Obama’s comments over the weekend. “Guys like Obama, they would pass the front door, they would see the broken masonry… He doesn’t notice dirt and filth where the walls haven’t been cleaned for years,” Trump told reporters as he headed for his latest midterm election rally. Cheesecake Factory is a popular restaurant chain known for its lengthy list of indulgent dishes and an eclectic interior design. Obama made a series of scathing criticisms of Republican Trump’s “chaos and cruelty” as he hit the stump for Democrats in Ohio and Michigan ahead of next week’s midterm elections. But it was Obama’s jabs at billionaire Trump’s prized renovations at the White House — including building a massive ballroom and adding gold-leafed ornamentation throughout the Oval Office — that really appeared to sting. “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said on Saturday, referring to the Iraqi dictator who was executed in 2006 following the US invasion of Iraq. Trump has long had a bitter rivalry with Obama. He launched his own political career by pushing the racist and false “birther” conspiracy theory that the Democrat was lying about being born in the United States. But Trump’s rant over the cheesecake comments was also a sign of the 80-year-old’s increasingly short temper as the midterms loom. On Sunday night, Trump sent his longest ever post on his Truth Social network — a 1,300-word screed in which he railed not about Iran or the economy but about US comedian Bill Maher. Last week Trump also lashed out at a series of reporters as he faced questions about the midterms, in which Republicans face losing control of Congress, and his dealings with Russia. item.title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Spain’s Luis de la Fuente wins men’s Coach of the Year award
item.description: Spain national team manager Luis de la Fuente has won the Men’s Coach of the Year award at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony after leading Spain to victory at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. De la Fuente emerged victorious ahead of fellow nominees Mikel Arteta of Arsenal, Luis Enrique of Paris Saint-Germain, Vincent Kompany of Bayern Munich and Unai Emery of Aston Villa. Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez presented the award, although the announcement was briefly interrupted by an unexpected mix-up involving the winner’s name on the card. Benitez eventually announced De la Fuente as the winner, prompting the Spanish coach to shake hands with Emery and Spain international Lamine Yamal before making his way to the stage. The award adds to De la Fuente’s achievements with the Spanish national team, following Spain’s triumph at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. item.title: [UPDATED] Ebola: Nigeria Has 54 Primary Contacts Now, Many Are In Quarantine, Says NCDC
item.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) on Monday said that it has identified another contact linked to the confirmed case of the recent Ebola outbreak in Nigeria, increasing the number of primary contacts to 54. The Director-General of the agency, Dr. Jide Idris, disclosed this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , identifying the new contact as an e-hailing driver who drove the index patient. “So as it is now, we’ve had — yesterday it was 54, right? One has left. The index case has left, so we had 53. “Today, we got one more suspected case contact, who actually was the Uber driver who actually drove her again before to the first hospital. That information we got later,” he said. ﻿ Idris explained that many of the contacts were in quarantine, including six who self-quarantined at home. “So we still have 54 contacts, primary contacts. What we do is that we follow up with these people because a lot of them are in quarantine right now somewhere in Abuja, here, about 40-something of them.” “We have six that are home, self-quarantined because the risks appear low. But they monitor them, call them, take their temperature, morning, evening, just to ensure that there are no changes in clinical situation. “And one or two cases like that we had. He changes. And we had to do, we had to test them again. And the three of them again today were tested, and all the three of them turned out negative,” he added. Not Out Of The Woods The NCDC chief also said efforts were ongoing to identify the secondary contacts. “So we are not out of the woods yet until we are sure that we have all the contacts, and they have been followed up. So we are still not out of the woods; because the index case is out doesn’t mean that we don’t have that,” added. The DG further said that though Nigeria does not have an active positive case, there are contacts that the agency needs to follow up. “Anyone who is symptomatic will test to be sure. You have to follow them for between two and 21 days. That’s the incubation period. And again, after 21 days, you follow up 21 days again. You take it to that before you say, OK, this is Ebola-free,” Idris said. “And after 21 days you test again, it’s negative, you can allow them to go. For secondary contacts, we don’t know how many until we start taking them.” Asked what anyone who experiences symptoms should do, the DG said, “Contact the nearest public health centre. There is an NCDC number: 6232. It is a hotline. item.title: NDC opens new Abuja base, targets 2027 electoral victory
item.description: …As Dickson hails new national secretariat as Noah’s Ark 2 By Henry Umoru The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has inaugurated its newly acquired national secretariat in Abuja as part of efforts to strengthen its operations ahead of the 2027 general election. The facility, located in the Jabi area of the Federal Capital Territory, was unveiled shortly after an emergency meeting of the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC), as it marks a significant step in the party’s efforts to strengthen its organisational structure and establish a permanent administrative base as preparations for the forthcoming elections gather momentum. The new secretariat is expected to serve as the party’s administrative centre and headquarters for its presidential campaign as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum, just as the development marks a step in the NDC’s efforts to establish a permanent national base for coordinating its activities and managing its expanding political structure. It is a strategic centre for coordinating its activities, strengthening communication among state chapters and mobilising supporters across the country and is also expected to play a central role in organising the party’s presidential campaign and coordinating other electoral activities ahead of the 2027 general elections In his remarks, the National Leader of the party, Senator Seriake Dickson, described the facility as its new “Noah’s Ark” ahead of the 2027 general elections as he congratulated members and supporters on the acquisition, describing the new secretariat as a unifying centre that would provide a befitting home for the party’s growing membership. He referred to the facility as the NDC’s newly acquired “Noah’s Ark,” a description underscoring its importance as a rallying point for members and supporters as the party pursues its political ambitions. The inauguration attracted the party’s National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas; National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson; and Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly. Also present was the party’s Rivers State governorship candidate, Dumo Lulu-Briggs, alongside other party leaders and members. With this, the NDC has positioned itself as an alternative political platform for Nigerians seeking a change from the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). With the new facility, the party is expected to strengthen coordination between its national leadership, state chapters and other structures as election preparations continue. item.title: OPHK troops destroy ISWAP enclaves in Lake Chad, kill 16 terrorists
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Hadin Kai have neutralised 16 suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters during coordinated air and artillery strikes on three suspected terrorist locations in the Tunbunma area of South Lake Chad, following intelligence on the presence of key terrorist leaders and fighters. According to the Joint Task Force, the operation followed sustained and relentless offensive against terrorist networks in the Lake Chad Basin. “The operation was conducted between 1 am and 2 am on 26 October 2026, using air and ground weapon systems to engage the identified locations. “Battle Damage Assessment indicates that 16 ISWAP fighters were neutralised across the targeted locations. “Among those reportedly killed were Abu Zubiru, an Arab national, and two associates, Baana Nglewa and Jindullah Sadiq, alongside other fighters. “Additionally, Abu Saleem, identified as the Wali of Tunbunma, sustained severe injuries alongside seven others. “Operation Hadin Kai reaffirms that there is no hiding place for terrorists and remains committed to restoring peace and normalcy while conducting intelligence-led operations against terrorist elements in the North East. “Members of the public are encouraged to provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing counter-terrorism operations.” The post OPHK troops destroy ISWAP enclaves in Lake Chad, kill 16 terrorists appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to 60,000 staff
item.description: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, the company said on Monday, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant seeks to cut costs while pouring money into artificial intelligence. Staff on select teams in the United States, Canada, India and Britain at vice president level and below will be eligible, a Microsoft spokesperson said, while some groups of employees, including some working on data centers, sales and marketing, are excluded. “The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter,” Amy Coleman, an executive vice president and chief people officer, told employees in a memo. It’s the second voluntary buyout offer that Microsoft has offered employees this year. In April, the company reportedly offered around seven percent of its US workforce the option to retire early. Around 30 percent of those eligible took the voluntary retirement plan, according to CNBC. Microsoft had 223,000 employees globally at the end of June, down from 228,000 at the end of 2025, according to regulatory filings. Around 27 percent of Microsoft’s workforce is eligible for the new buyout offer. The company is expected to report quarterly earnings later this week. item.title: Niger APC raises 525-member campaign council, targets 2m votes for Tinubu/Bago
item.description: By Clare Nnabuike Niger State Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago has declared that his party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), is targeting 2 million votes to defeat the opposition parties in the 2027 presidential and governorship elections. The governor made this known on Monday at the inauguration of a 525-member State Presidential/Gubernatorial Campaign Council of the APC in Minna, where he revealed that the council is drawn from commissioners, special advisers, local government chairmen, councillors, state and national lawmakers, ministers, directors-general and coordinators. Bago described the structure as spanning party units to the state level and including political appointees, with total membership exceeding 100,000 over the years. “If everybody would bring its own votes, it would give us more than 1 million votes. But our target is beyond that. The ambition this time around is to bring out over 2 million votes, and by the grace of God we will do that,” he said. The governor urged the party to welcome returnees who had earlier defected to other parties, crediting the APC’s emergence as a coalition of parties that defeated the main opposition. He called for constructive media coverage and warned against overheating the polity or triggering insecurity, saying the campaign would highlight the federal government’s economic policies, improved revenue and job creation. Bago cited recent infrastructure and security gains, including better roads and freer movement of goods in parts of the state, as part of what the government has done and disclosed that the North Central Presidential Campaign office in Minna would be commissioned next week, with possible attendance of the President, Vice President, Senate President, Speaker or National Chairman. Minister of Information, Idris Malagi, in his remarks, praised the choice of leadership of the council and said the APC would campaign on the administration’s record of transforming the Nigerian economy over the past three and a half years. He urged the newly appointed members to prioritise the collective good of the state and party unity The chairman of the APC North Central, Hon. Mu’azu Rijau, while congratulating the council leadership, stressed that the 2027 campaign council should not underestimate opponents, saying the party aimed to re-elect Governor Bago alongside its senators, House of Representatives members and state assembly members. Director-General of the campaign council, Ahmed Ibeto, accepted the assignment on behalf of members, pledging hard work, strategic coordination, grassroots engagement, unity, discipline and compliance with electoral guidelines. He said the council would establish operational frameworks across directorates, local governments, wards and units, and would value experience while welcoming new ideas. item.title: Temwa Chawinga becomes first African woman to finish in Ballon d’Or top 10
item.description: Malawian forward Temwa Chawinga has made history by becoming the first African woman to finish in the top 10 of the women’s Ballon d’Or. Chawinga’s achievement marks a significant milestone for African women’s football, placing the Malawi international among the world’s leading female players. Born on September 20, 1998, in Rumphi District, Malawi, Chawinga plays as a forward for Kansas City Current and the Malawi national team. She has enjoyed considerable success at club level, winning four Chinese Women’s Super League titles with Wuhan Jianghan University in 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023. She also won the NWSL x Liga MX Femenil Summer Cup in 2024 and the NWSL Shield in 2025 with Kansas City Current. Her individual honours include two consecutive NWSL Most Valuable Player awards in 2024 and 2025, as well as two NWSL Golden Boots in the same years. Chawinga also claimed the Chinese Women’s Super League Golden Boot in 2022 and 2023 before winning the International Federation of Football History and Statistics (IFFHS) World’s Best Top Goal Scorer award in 2023. She was joined in the Ballon d’Or top 10 by Haiti’s Melchie Dumornay, Norway’s Caroline Graham Hansen, Spain’s Patri Guijarro, Denmark’s Pernille Harder, Poland’s Ewa Pajor, Spain’s Clàudia Pina and Alexia Putellas, England’s Alessia Russo, and Jamaica’s Khadija Shaw. The list features players from Europe, Africa and the Caribbean, reflecting the growing global reach of women’s football. Chawinga’s historic finish represents a breakthrough for African representation in the prestigious individual award and further highlights her rise as one of the leading figures in the women’s game. item.title: Police confirm man, teenager swept away by flood in Aba
item.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Police Command has confirmed that a man who attempted to rescue a teenage girl from a water-filled ditch at Faulks Road, Aba, was swept away alongside the girl during Sunday’s downpour. The Police Public Relations Officer, Maureen Chinaka, disclosed this while responding to Vanguard inquiries, confirming that the incident occurred around the popular Ukwu Mango area of the commercial city. Chinaka said the tragedy happened near an ongoing construction site where an uncovered ditch had filled with rainwater. According to her, the teenage girl was passing through the area when she reportedly hit a stone and fell into the ditch. An adult who witnessed the incident reportedly plunged into the water in an attempt to rescue her, but both were swept away. “Unfortunately, we have not been able to see them. The police are aware, and the matter has been reported. Efforts are in place to see how they can be rescued,” Chinaka said. She confirmed that the two victims had yet to be found as search efforts continued. Asked whether the construction company responsible for the site would face possible charges over negligence, the police spokesperson said investigations were ongoing. The tragedy has raised concerns about the safety of construction sites during heavy rainfall, particularly where excavations and drainage channels are left uncovered and become submerged in floodwater. Aba’s flat terrain makes parts of the commercial city vulnerable to flooding during heavy downpours, increasing the risks posed by waterlogged roads, open drains and excavations. item.title: Impunity, justice system failure fuelling violence in North Central — Osinbajo
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa Former Vice President of Nigeria, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo, has attributed the widespread insecurity in North Central Nigeria and other parts of the country to failures in the justice system and inadequate punitive measures for crimes committed. Osinbajo stated this on Monday in Plateau State at a forum titled, “Countering Polarisation and Rebuilding Civic Cohesion in North Central Nigeria Beyond Tribe and Faith, Reclaiming Our Shared Stories,” organised by Justice Research Institute, JRI, in partnership with the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies, NIPSS. The former Vice President said, “Impunity destroys the fabric of society. There must be clear and enforceable consequences for wrongdoing and offences committed against the state or individuals.” “If there are no consequences for actions taken under any guise, there will be no way to rebuild and reconcile. Peace cannot be built without justice.” “Those who have been displaced and whose communities or villages have been illegally occupied must be returned to their ancestral homes. Victims must also be compensated.” “If you look at the land-grabbing situation, land must be returned to its rightful owners. “ “This is the process of rebuilding. There must be compensation, the proper procedure must be followed, and any wrongdoing must result in a penalty. “The problems of justice administration in Nigeria require urgent attention in the form of reforms to address the majority of the issues impeding justice delivery.” “It is better for the country to recognise that we have a system that requires immediate intervention.” “For peace to reign, we must reorient our attitudes towards ourselves and others, particularly our brothers and sisters. I believe we should return to the basics, and this should be done intentionally.” He added, “Reconciliation must be deliberate and genuine. Regardless of what happened in Rwanda, they are back together because leaders and governments made a deliberate and intentional effort to bring people together. “I believe there is a need for deliberate and intentional reconciliation and peace-building, which can only be accomplished by government in collaboration with civil society organisations and religious leaders. “Many of these will be determined by our country’s elite.” In his welcome address, the Director-General of NIPSS, Prof. Ayo Omotayo, said, “Storytelling is a powerful instrument for peace-building and national reconciliation. “Societies are held together not only by laws and institutions but also by the stories citizens tell about themselves and one another.” “Stories shape our memories, influence how we understand our differences and imagine our common future.” “They can inspire solidarity, but when distorted or manipulated, they can deepen grievances and turn neighbours into enemies.” Also speaking, the former Chief Justice and Emir of Lafia, Justice Sidi Bage, said, “Conflict often begins long before violence erupts. item.title: El Niño: What it means and how Nigerians should prepare
item.description: By Sekinat Osundiji Nigeria may experience increased heat and changing rainfall patterns as a strengthening El Niño event raises concerns about its potential effects on agriculture, water supply, electricity generation and public health. The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) said in September 2026 that El Niño was expected to strengthen into a very strong event and persist into early 2027. The Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) has also warned that the phenomenon could affect rainfall patterns, including the length of the rainy season and when it ends. But what is El Niño, how could it affect Nigeria, and what can the country do to prepare? What is El Niño? El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon that occurs when surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become warmer than average. This warming affects atmospheric circulation, changing weather patterns around the world. Depending on the region, it can contribute to higher temperatures, reduced or excessive rainfall, and shifts in seasonal conditions. El Niño is part of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), a climate pattern that also includes La Niña, its cooler phase, and neutral conditions. According to the WMO, El Niño typically occurs every two to seven years and lasts between nine and 12 months. Although it develops thousands of kilometres from Nigeria, its influence on global atmospheric circulation can affect weather in West Africa. However, its effects vary by location and do not automatically mean drought or extreme heat everywhere. What does El Niño mean for Nigeria? NiMet’s August 2026 seasonal climate update identified the onset of a strong El Niño event and outlined possible implications for rainfall, agriculture, water resources and energy. For August to October 2026, the agency forecast normal to above-normal rainfall across much of northern Nigeria, while parts of the South-West and Cross River State were expected to experience normal to below-normal rainfall. These projections highlight the possibility of different weather outcomes across the country. 1. Higher temperatures and health risks One major concern is the possibility of increased heat. In October 2026, the Climate Impact Lab projected that Nigeria could record an additional 31,400 heat-related deaths between September 2026 and February 2027, compared with an average year. The figure is a model-based estimate of potential excess deaths, not a confirmed death toll or a certainty that those deaths will occur. Extreme heat can cause dehydration, heat exhaustion and potentially fatal heatstroke, particularly among children, older people and outdoor workers. Health authorities should strengthen public awareness campaigns, issue timely heat warnings and prepare health facilities for heat-related emergencies.
